notes: Owner ordered a Rev 3 of the 3-node cluster architecture under three constraints: stay inside Always Free, every VM directly reachable, recovery two-way. Rev 3 is an overlay on Rev 2 and deletes nothing. It corrects four Rev 2 defects found against live infrastructure: Desktop Commander has no inbound agent port, the estate is one VCN and one 10.0.0.0/24 rather than a two-subnet 10.20.x design, no section required a backup to exist, and R0-R3 was a second governance vocabulary with no mapping to authority_class. Requirement 3 conflicted with Rev 2 section 4.1's deliberate one-way recovery rule; resolved as bidirectional in capability and asymmetric in privilege. dial-hermes-control gains a BOUNDED_RECOVERY role capped at R1 over a distinct forced-command, source-restricted identity with no credential loop, closing the both-E2s-down gap that was the actual 2026-09-12 situation. It never gains R2 or R3, and R2 and above require owner authorization in either direction. The bound is enforced at three layers, of which only the forced command on the target does not depend on the caller's cooperation. Also completes the offsite evidence backup started earlier: allowlisted content, credential-scanned, drive.file-scoped, inert until the owner authorizes Drive once. No change to product, money, security authority or owner-control intent. Two-way recovery is built and unit-tested but has never run between two live hosts; Rev 3 section 9.2 states that rather than claiming it is proven.
